conflict_topics: Leave requests for the working day before Hari Raya (first day)
Leave requests for the working day after Hari Raya (second day)
Holiday coverage burden and Christmas rostering (side issue)
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers provide concrete, personal reasons (childcare, family trip, religious preparation) which structure negotiation ('My kid's childcare centre is closed.' Turn 2; 'family's got a trip planned.' Turn 1; 'we use that day to prepare for Hari Raya.' Turn 16).
Negotiation proceeds through explicit offers and confirmations rather than vague promises (D: 'I'll work with Agent C on the first day.' Turn 22; C: 'Okay. So I'll do Hari Raya' Turn 9).
Little needless repetition; positions are restated when contested but not obfuscated.
evaluation.final_reason: Concrete staffing agreement: Agent C had volunteered to 'do Hari Raya' (Turn 9) and Agent D then committed to work the first day with Agent C ('I'll work with Agent C on the first day.' Turn 22). That arrangement provides two staff (C and D) on duty, which allows Agent A and Agent B to take the requested day off. Evidence: D's explicit offer and A/B acceptance—A: 'Oh. Thanks, Agent D. That works then.' (Turn 23).
position_change_notes: Agent C shifted from a complaint ('I've covered every public holiday for the last two years.' Turn 3) to an explicit offer to cover Hari Raya ('I can work the Hari Raya days.' Turn 7; 'I'll do Hari Raya.' Turn 9).
Agent B softened their demand about the second day ('I can work the second day.' Turn 6) while keeping the first day as essential due to childcare constraints.

Agent D ultimately changed from requesting Hari Raya leave (Turn 4) to accommodating others by offering to work the first day and by covering Christmas as needed ('I'll work with Agent C on the first day.' Turn 22; 'I can work Christmas.' Turn 8).

Agent A initially requested both days (Turn 1) and conceded Hari Raya to D earlier in the conversation ('Okay, Agent D, for Hari Raya... that's fair enough.' Turn 5) while retaining the need for the first day until the final arrangement.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A and Agent B both report having 'put in' for the same days (Turn 1-2), creating an incompatible set of leave requests for the same dates.
Agent C notes covering every public holiday (Turn 3), implying burden and potential objection, and Agent D also requests the Hari Raya days (Turn 4) — now three staff have overlapping claims.

Agent A concedes Hari Raya to Agent D ('Okay, Agent D, for Hari Raya... that's fair enough.' Turn 5) and Agent B offers to work the second day (Turn 6), reducing but not eliminating the dispute over the first day.

Agent C volunteers to work the Hari Raya days but requests Christmas off (Turn 7); Agent D can work Christmas (Turn 8). This negotiates away the holiday coverage issue but leaves the first-day staffing unresolved.
Agent C confirms 'I'll do Hari Raya' and Agent D accepts (Turn 9-10). D then asks who will work with C on the first day (Turn 10), leaving the core staffing question for that first day open.
Agent A states they 'need that first day too' (Turn 11) and Agent B responds they have no one for childcare that day (Turn 12), making the first-day claim explicit from both parties.
Both A and B reiterate exclusionary reasons (A: family trip starts then, Turn 13; B: mother only available on second day, Turn 14), maintaining the clear disagreement over the first day.
Agent D adds that the first day is important for Hari Raya preparation (Turn 16), so three staff (A, B, D) claim the same first day; Agent A notes 'three of us who need that first day' (Turn 17).

A normative dispute about legitimacy continues (B: 'A holiday isn't the same as having no one to look after your kid.' Turn 18; A: 'It's a family plan...not simple for me to change.' Turn 19) with no settlement.

Agent D concedes operationally and offers to work: 'If you have no one for your kid, you should take the day. I'll work with Agent C on the first day.' (Turns 22). This, together with C's earlier confirmation to do Hari Raya, fixes staffing for the first day (C and D working) and allows both A and B to have the day off.
Agent A accepts the arrangement and thanks Agent D ('Oh. Thanks, Agent D. That works then.' Turn 23), indicating no remaining substantive disagreement.
Post-resolution appreciation between B and D ('Agent D, thank you...That's a huge help.' Turn 26-27). No new substantive conflict appears.

substantive_insights: Conflict centered on overlapping, legitimate personal obligations (childcare, family travel, religious preparation) rather than a single 'entitled' claim — this required a practical staffing solution rather than an appeal to policy.
An effective resolution came when staff who could cover the shift explicitly committed to working (C and D), rather than through arbitration or rule-based priority.
Secondary trade-offs appeared (C accepting Hari Raya coverage in exchange for Christmas off), showing how unrelated scheduling needs were negotiated as part of a broader roster solution.
